What gets blocked and tips for the best results
One domain per line. Subdomains are included.

The app stops lookups to known ad and tracking servers across your whole phone – in apps, games and browsers. It uses a local VPN: all traffic stays on the phone and only DNS lookups pass through the app, so your speed is not affected.

These apps load ads from the same servers as their regular content, so no blocker of this type can remove them without breaking the apps. What works:
• Firefox with the uBlock Origin add-on
• Samsung Internet with an ad blocker
• YouTube Premium

Turn off \"Use secure DNS\" in Chrome (Settings → Privacy and security) and set Android\'s \"Private DNS\" to Off or Automatic, otherwise the browser can bypass blocking. Ads that a website serves from its own servers cannot be blocked this way.
Ads from AdMob, Unity Ads, AppLovin, ironSource, Vungle, Facebook and others are blocked. In-game rewards for watching ads will stop working.
Settings → Advanced → Always on. Choose L-AD Blocker and turn on \"Always-on VPN\" so protection starts automatically, even after a restart.
Go to Activity, tap the red domain and choose Allow.
Android allows only one VPN at a time. Starting another VPN turns blocking off.

Version %1$s

L-AD Blocker removes ads and tracking across your phone by filtering lookups to ad servers directly on the device.

The app does not collect any data. Lookups that are not blocked are sent to the DNS server you chose in Settings.

Blocklists: HaGeZi, StevenBlack, AdAway and OISD.
L-AD Blocker uses a local VPN to stop ads. No traffic is sent to any external server.\n\nIf another VPN app is active, turn it off and try again.
